title: Sundar Scored 52, Bowled Eight Overs, and Got Named in Three Squads. This Is Not Ashwin's Replacement. This Is India's New All-Rounder.
excerpt: Washington Sundar's unbeaten half-century and tidy bowling against Afghanistan cap a 12-month rise from fringe player to India's most trusted spin all-rounder across all three formats.
body:
Washington Sundar walked off the field at the New PCA Stadium on Sunday afternoon with 52 not out from 68 balls. Captain Shubman Gill had just declared at 564 for 8. A few hours later, Sundar had the ball in his hand, probing Afghanistan's middle order alongside debutant Manav Suthar. By stumps, Afghanistan were 113 for 5 and Sundar had bowled 8 overs for 27 runs without a wicket — tidy, accurate, exactly what the team needed while Suthar and Prasidh Krishna did the damage.

It was a quiet, complete day's work. The kind Ravichandran Ashwin used to deliver with metronomic regularity for a decade. The kind India have been searching for since Ashwin and Ravindra Jadeja last played a home Test together — 69 consecutive matches in which at least one of them always featured.

## The Audition That Became a Permanent Role

Sundar's journey to this point has been anything but linear. He debuted for India as a 17-year-old T20 specialist in 2017. He played the Gabba Test in 2021, scoring 62 in a famous win, then disappeared from Test squads for three years — a victim of injuries, squad depth, and the long shadows cast by Ashwin and Jadeja.

When both veterans retired from international cricket, Sundar was not the obvious heir. He was 25, had played barely a handful of Tests, and was seen primarily as a white-ball cricketer. His county stint with Hampshire in England changed the calculus. He took wickets on English pitches, scored runs in the middle order, and returned to India with a résumé that demanded attention.

The Anderson-Tendulkar Trophy series against England in early 2025 was the turning point. At The Oval, with India staring at a series-levelling defeat, Sundar walked in at 181 for 6 and scored 53 off 46 balls, including four sixes. His batting intelligence — restraint when the last man joined him, then explosive acceleration — gave India just enough to defend. His childhood coach, M. Senthilnathan, put it plainly: "He is perfectly fitting in the role of what Ashwin did for so long with Jadeja."

## The Numbers Back the Eye Test

Sundar's Test batting average of 38.92 would stand up in any middle order. His six half-centuries in 11 Tests — now including Sunday's 52 not out against Afghanistan — show a player who converts starts. He has scored at least 50 in almost every Test he has played, a consistency that suggests he does not just have talent but the temperament to apply it when the team needs him.

His bowling figures in this match were modest — 8-1-27-0 — but his role was containment while Suthar attacked. He bowled dry, gave nothing away, and created the pressure from which wickets fell at the other end. It is the same dual function Ashwin performed for years: bat in the top seven, bowl 20 overs in the right areas, hold catches.

## Selected Everywhere, Trusted Fully

The timing of Sundar's performance could not have been better. On Saturday, the BCCI announced India's squads for the Ireland T20Is, the England T20Is, and the 2026 Asian Games. Sundar was named in all three. He is one of only a handful of Indian cricketers currently trusted across all formats — a distinction that speaks to both his versatility and the selectors' belief in his all-round capabilities.

For NRI cricket fans who grew up watching Ashwin and Jadeja own Indian home pitches, the transition has been anxious. Would anyone step up? Would India's spin-dependent home strategy survive? Sundar's emergence — not as a flashy replacement but as a competent, reliable successor — is the most reassuring answer the team has offered.

## What Comes Next

India need nine wickets on Day 3 to finish this Test. Afghanistan, trailing by 451, face an uphill battle to avoid the follow-on. Sundar will almost certainly bowl a long spell. If the pitch continues to offer turn, his off-spin, combined with Suthar's left-arm variety and Kuldeep Yadav's wrist spin, gives Gill three distinct spinning options.

After this match, India will play three ODIs against Afghanistan before Sundar flies to Ireland with the T20 squad. It will be a long summer — Ireland, England, then the Asian Games in Japan in September. For a cricketer who spent three years on the fringes, it is a schedule that reflects how far he has come. Not as a stand-in, but as a starter.
